ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Babe Didrikson Zaharias

code.originalText: After nine doses: final restaging, clinical complete response, and the watch-and-wait surveillance plan

text.paragraph: Final restaging after nine doses of dostarlimab. [S]

Ms. Didrikson Zaharias returns two weeks after her ninth and last dose of dostarlimab. Final restaging last week showed only fibrosis on MRI, no metastases on CT, and a flat white scar with no ulcer on sigmoidoscopy. She has had no bleeding, urgency or change in bowel habit for five months, and no diarrhea, rash, cough or breathlessness. She takes levothyroxine 75 micrograms each morning, has no tiredness or cold intolerance, and is still taking ferrous sulfate. The second hepatitis B vaccine dose was given with the last dose of dostarlimab. She played four tournaments over the summer and won a regional event last month. She asked what watch-and-wait means and how she will know if the cancer comes back. [S]

tr.td: Fit and well; weight 63.4 kg; blood pressure 112/70, pulse 64
Soft, non-tender; no liver enlargement or mass
With her agreement and a chaperone: smooth, supple wall; no mass, nodule or ulcer; normal sphincter tone; no blood

Bright red blood with bowel movements for about three months, with narrower stools, urgency, a feeling of incomplete emptying, and a firm, ulcerated mass felt on the back wall of the lower rectum at about 5 cm from the anal verge: a rectal cancer must be confirmed or excluded. Colonoscopy with biopsy booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented fatigue before her cancer diagnosis. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic rectal blood loss: hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL, MCV 77 fL, ferritin 9 ng/mL, with tiredness
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the documented fatigue at the end of the 1952 season.

Adenocarcinoma of the low rectum, mismatch repair deficient (loss of MSH2 and MSH6; microsatellite instability high), cT3bN1M0 (stage IIIB) on pelvic MRI, lower edge 4 cm from the anal verge and about 1 cm above the anorectal junction, mesorectal fascia clear, no extramural venous invasion; CEA 5.8 ng/mL; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose site the sources do not record exactly
S — Synthetic histology, site, stage, mismatch repair status and course; the sources say she had cancer treated with a colostomy and call it colon cancer (R on the site). See sources.md.

Acute viral upper respiratory infection with cough and sore throat, a week before cycle 4 of dostarlimab; oxygen saturation and chest X-ray normal, so immune-related pneumonitis is unlikely; rapid influenza and COVID-19 tests negative; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

Immune-related primary hypothyroidism from dostarlimab, grade 2: tiredness and cold hands, TSH 12.6 mIU/L and free T4 0.6 ng/dL after four doses, following a mild TSH rise four weeks earlier; dostarlimab continued
S — Synthetic common immune-related adverse event of PD-1 blockade.

list.item:
Low rectal adenocarcinoma, mismatch repair deficient, after dostarlimab: clinical complete response (C20). Clinical complete response on all three tests that define it: a normal rectal examination, a flat white scar without ulcer or nodularity on endoscopy, and only fibrosis without restricted diffusion on MRI; CT shows no metastases and CEA is 1.6 ng/mL. With the tumor board, she chose watch-and-wait: no radiation and no surgery, with close surveillance so that any regrowth can be removed early. She keeps her rectum and anus, and will not need a colostomy unless the tumor regrows. [S]
Watch-and-wait: rectal examination and sigmoidoscopy every three to four months and pelvic MRI every six months for two years.
CEA every three to six months; CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis every six to twelve months; colonoscopy at one year.
Written survivorship care plan given today.
Screening advice for first-degree relatives repeated.

Immune-related primary hypothyroidism on levothyroxine (E03.2). TSH 2.4 mIU/L and free T4 1.2 ng/dL on levothyroxine 75 micrograms; symptoms gone. The TSH due with the ninth dose was not drawn. [S]
Continue levothyroxine 75 micrograms.
TSH in six months, then yearly.

Iron deficiency anemia from rectal blood loss (D50.0). Hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL and ferritin 41 ng/mL: anemia corrected and stores partly refilled. [S]
Ferrous sulfate for three more months, then stop.
Blood count with the next surveillance visit.
